problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.$
- If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & \,0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.$
- If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=1.$
- If $B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=2.$
- If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is true. The matrix $A$ has $1$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot column. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- Statement II is true. The matrix $B$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=2.
$$

- Statement III is false. The matrix $C$ has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
